title: Viện trợ tiền mặt hay hàng hóa · Agree / Disagree
prompt: Some people believe that giving disaster-affected households cash instead of donated goods where markets still function is a sensible approach. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

source.detail: Bài luyện mở rộng biên soạn riêng cho năm 2026. Tham khảo các nhóm chủ đề trong forecast công khai; tình huống, bài mẫu và phân tích được viết mới.
source.disclaimer: Không xác nhận đề này đã xuất hiện hoặc sẽ xuất hiện trong kỳ thi. Các chủ đề ngách được bổ sung để mở rộng phạm vi luyện tập; không gán xác suất ra thi.

keywords: Viện trợ tiền mặt hay hàng hóa Hỗ trợ tiền mặt có thể để hộ giải quyết nhu cầu gói cứu trợ tiêu chuẩn không dự liệu bởi vì gia đình biết thiếu hụt trước mắt là vận chuyển, thuốc hay loại thực phẩm cụ thể. Minh họa: Hộ có trẻ sơ sinh có thể mua vật dụng phù hợp tại chỗ thay vì nhận thêm chăn không cần. Không suy rộng từ ví dụ thành bảo đảm thành công cho tất cả.
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.
paragraphs: After a disaster, standard parcels may be easy for agencies to distribute while failing to match the varied needs of affected households. I broadly agree with the proposal, but my support rests on a clear distinction: recipient choice is valuable only when necessary goods can actually be obtained at reasonable prices.

Cash assistance can let households address needs that standard relief parcels do not anticipate. The mechanism is straightforward: families know whether their immediate shortage concerns transport, medicine or a specific type of food. For example, a household with an infant could buy suitable supplies locally instead of receiving another blanket it does not need. Buying locally can also restore ordinary trade, although this benefit disappears if payments merely chase the same limited stock at higher prices.

Cash may lose purchasing power if traders cannot replenish stock after roads or warehouses are damaged. Aid agencies should assess supply conditions and combine cash with direct deliveries when local shortages persist. Cash transfers also require a safe delivery route that the intended recipient controls. A payment reaching a household account may not reach the person who buys essential supplies, so agencies need confidential feedback and accessible alternatives rather than assuming that the nominal recipient can always decide how the money is spent. This qualification is essential because recipient choice is valuable only when necessary goods can actually be obtained at reasonable prices.

I support cash relief where supply and payment systems make genuine choice possible. Agencies should retain direct deliveries when essential goods are scarce and verify that recipients control the money, so a flexible transfer meets varied needs rather than merely shifting responsibility for impossible purchases onto affected families.
